1 Introduction

In this hypothetical situation (the data is made up, i.e. does not exist), Carrefour Rome is planning on launching a coupon program designed to increase revenue by providing discount coupon for purchases over 40 euros. So they have funding to run a randomized controlled trial (RCT) in some stores They selected about a 70% of their stores in Rome and they want to investigate whether offering coupons has any effect on revenue.

Thus, we want to calculate \(E(\text{Post-Treatment revenue | Coupon})\)

In a first instance, we create the relationship among the many different variables:

2 Inspecting the Area

Let’s assume that the experiment has been conducted and the data has come in. Let us first have a first look at the area where Carrefour ran the experiment.

Question 1

Produce the same map in leaflet.

library("leaflet")
library("leaflegend")

#name <- colorFactor(topo.colors(3), domain = carrefour$name) 
pal <- 
   colorFactor(palette = c("blue", "red", "purple"), 
               levels = c("Carrefour Express", "Carrefour Market", "Carrefour Iper"))


leaflet(carrefour) %>% addTiles() %>%
  addCircleMarkers(lng = ~lon_x, lat = ~lat_y, 
             popup = ~address, radius = 4, color = ~pal(name))%>%
  addLegendFactor(
    pal=pal,
    values = carrefour$name,
    position = 'topright',
    shape = 'circle',
    width = 10,
    height = 10,
    opacity = .5)%>%
  addScaleBar(
  position = c("bottomright"))

Question 3

Create a static map that displays the stores that got treated vs. not.

ggplot()+
  geom_sf(data = roads, color = "grey", linewidth=0.1)+
    geom_point(data = carrefour, aes(x=lon_x, y=lat_y, color = treat))+
    coord_sf(xlim = c(min_lon_x, max_lon_x), ylim = c(min_lat_y, max_lat_y), expand = FALSE)+
        ggspatial::annotation_scale(location = 'tr')+
    theme_bw()+
  labs(x = "Longitude", y="Latitude")

Question 6

Create graphs that compare the pointrange for the treatment and control groups for the following variables:

  • variety of products
  • store size
  • traffic
  • pre-treatment income
plot_variety_products <- ggplot(carrefour, aes(x = treat, y = variety_products, color = treat)) +
  stat_summary(geom = "pointrange", fun.data = "mean_se", fun.args = list(mult = 1.96)) +
  guides(color = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Variety products")

plot_store_size <- ggplot(carrefour, aes(x = treat, y = store_size, color = treat)) +
  stat_summary(geom = "pointrange", fun.data = "mean_se", fun.args = list(mult = 1.96)) +
  guides(color = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Store Size")

plot_traffic <- ggplot(carrefour, aes(x = treat, y = traffic, color = treat)) +
  stat_summary(geom = "pointrange", fun.data = "mean_se", fun.args = list(mult = 1.96)) +
  guides(color = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Traffic")


plot_revenue_pre <- ggplot(carrefour, aes(x = treat, y = revenue_pre, color = treat)) +
  stat_summary(geom = "pointrange", fun.data = "mean_se", fun.args = list(mult = 1.96)) +
  guides(color = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Revenue - Pre Intervention")

ggarrange(plot_variety_products, plot_store_size, 
          plot_traffic, plot_revenue_pre, ncol=2, nrow=2, common.legend = TRUE)

Question 7

Create graphs that compare the distributions for the treatment and control groups for the following variables:

  • variety of products
  • store size
  • traffic
  • pre-treatment income
plot_diff_variety_products_d<-ggplot(carrefour, aes(x = variety_products, fill = treat, group=treat)) +
  guides(color = "none", alpha=0.5) +
  geom_histogram(color = "white",
                 alpha = 0.5)+
  #Adding density and multiplying by a manually defined value
  #for visibility
  geom_density(aes(y = after_stat(density)* 300, color=treat), 
               #alpha = 0.5,
               fill=NA)+
  #Adding a secondary axis
  scale_y_continuous(name = "count",
                     sec.axis = 
                       sec_axis(~.x/300, 
                                name = "density"))+
  labs(fill = NULL)+
  xlab(NULL)

plot_diff_store_size_d<-ggplot(carrefour, aes(x = store_size, fill = treat, group=treat)) +

Question 8

Are the treatment and the control group the same on pre-treatment covariates? Perform adequate tests and interpret them?

t.test(variety_products ~ coupon, data = carrefour, alternative=c("two.sided"))[3]
$p.value
[1] 0.4393249
t.test(store_size ~ coupon, data = carrefour, alternative=c("two.sided"))[3]
$p.value
[1] 0.3666812
t.test(traffic ~ coupon, data = carrefour, alternative=c("two.sided"))[3]
$p.value
[1] 0.2247868
t.test(revenue_pre ~ coupon, data = carrefour, alternative=c("two.sided"))[3]
$p.value
[1] 0.7520119

The results are not statistically significant.

Question 9

Estimate the difference: \(E(\text{Post-revenue | Coupon})\). What is the ATE? Calculate the average between the treatment and control group using means.

stores_randomized<-carrefour %>%
  group_by(treat) %>%
  summarize(avg_revenue_post = mean(revenue_post))
stores_randomized

That’s 65347.96 - 27285.94, or 38062.02, which means that the program caused an increase in revenue of 38062.02, on average.

Question 10

Calculate the difference between treatment and control groups using a regression. Make sure that the variables are labelled appropriately.

model_rct1 <- lm(revenue_post ~ treat, data = carrefour)

models<-list("Income" = model_rct1)

cm <- c('treatTreatment'='Offered Coupon (Treatment)',
        "(Intercept)"="Intercept")

modelsummary(models, stars = TRUE, coef_map = cm, gof_map = c("nobs", "r.squared"))

Question 13

What do you tell the Carrefour manager? Do the coupons work? Should Carrefour expand the coupon system?

Yes, the coupon system works. Offering the coupon system increased Carrerfour revenue by 27285.939 euros. It might be worth expanding the coupon system to larger areas.
